Soulframe: The RPG from the creators of Warframe opens its alpha to all PC players
items.summary: Soulframe, Digital Extremes’ multiplayer action RPG, opens its alpha to all PC players for free on November 6, 2026. The creators of Warframe are marking the occasion with an update focused on exploration, mounts and progression.
items.content:
After several years of testing limited to part of the community, Digital Extremes is opening Soulframe , its new multiplayer action RPG , published by the studio and playable on PC , for free starting November 6, 2026. The developers of Warframe announced the opening during a broadcast on October 30, with the aim of expanding testing and gathering more feedback on the game's systems. Dubbed Open Preludes , this phase lets players join the adventure without an invitation while development continues.

Soulframe showcases depict a fantasy world shaped by nature, fantastical creatures and territories affected by a form of corruption. Gameplay sequences highlight forest exploration, melee combat and interactions with animals.

The latest developer presentation focuses in particular on Verse of the Veilands , the update accompanying the start of testing. It details the new ways to get around and how certain regions change as players progress. Players will be able to restore corrupted areas and use a mount after completing several objectives.

Digital Extremes has not published a full story synopsis for this new testing phase. However, official information introduces the world of Midrath , a territory threatened by the forces of the Ode.

Players take on the role of Heralds , characters who travel across the region to fight corruption and restore their ties with the beings who inhabit it. As they progress, they can form pacts with various entities, meet characters, and complete narrative quests called Fables .

The story is gradually unfolding through updates. Its final trajectory and the full range of accessible regions are not yet known.

Unlike Warframe , which focuses primarily on ranged combat and fast-paced movement, Soulframe favors melee combat. Its combat system revolves around the use of weapons, specific abilities, and pacts that determine certain character skills.

Exploration also plays an important role. Players can explore the environments, search for resources, craft equipment and progress through various activities, including fishing. The game also features dynamic weather conditions and animal companions.

The adventure can be played solo or in co-op with up to four players . A matchmaking system also lets you find other players at certain shrines, including for exploring dungeons.

The main change on November 6, 2026 concerns access to the game. You will no longer need an invitation or to join the Founders Program to take part in the tests.

To get started, players will need to create an account on the official Soulframe website , then download the PC client. A Steam page is also available, but the game’s launch on the platform has not yet been dated.

The Verse of the Veilands update also introduces a world evolution system. After the The Tormented Stag quest, certain regions become accessible in a corrupted form. Players must purify them to continue progressing and unlock new activities.

Mounts are also making their debut. A young wolf can be raised and trained, then ridden once several conditions have been met. A new pact, Ode Shrike , adds abilities based in particular on traps, projectiles and chains that can be used to control opponents.

Finally, the return of the seasonal event Bita's Eve comes with a new mini-boss, Veltruska , while additional fishing activities are planned.

items.title: Soulframe Preview – Digital Extremes’ Warframe follow-up is ready to rule
items.summary: Digital Extremes’ journey through more than three decades of game development has been one marked with challenges, successes and a few failures, but in
items.content:
Digital Extremes’ journey through more than three decades of game development has been one marked with challenges, successes and a few failures, but in 2026 the company is arguably in the best position it’s ever been in. Warframe , its sci-fi ninja opus, is enjoying its best year – 14 years in from its original release, that feat is truly remarkable – and all the while it’s quietly tinkering away with its sword-and-sorcery follow-up, Soulframe .

Up till now, you’ve been able to experience the closed alpha test Soulframe Prelude only by invitation, but on November 6th they’re finally entering open beta. For the past three years, the team have maintained an open dialogue with its players and community, helping to build something that already feels pretty special. Now, though, it feels as though they’re ready to take the final steps towards the game’s full release, and, frankly, I couldn’t be more excited.

The game’s gloriously poetic opening sets an evocative tone, showcasing the emotional depth and poignancy that underlies Soulframe’s setting and outlook. Here, the Scottish narrator broadly leads your character development, but in the most unusual way, choosing traits for your mother as she cradles you in her arms. These are then inherited by your avatar as you meet them, bound and battered by an unknown Ode knight, before you’re dumped face-first into a pool wearing nothing but your grubby white underpants. Oh, and an intricate locked gauntlet that covers your entire arm. Seems odd, no?

You’re an Envoy, marked by the distinctive blue arm that lies beneath that gauntlet. As Soulframe leads you into its early systems, your next major milestone is choosing your Pact, with Courage, Grace or Spirit giving you the option between a melee, ranged or magic starting class, and then tailoring your equipment as you see fit. I was really interested in playing a ranged character, but decided to opt for a melee build, becoming a devotee of Tethren for my first time experiencing the game. You’ve got a batch of swords to choose from, and I went for a cool-looking sword and shield combo, with the ability to throw your shield and have it return to you, very much like a certain bearded God of War.

This is where it all begins. You’re dropped into the open world island of Midreth, part of the wider world of Alca, with a small number of enemies lurking in nearby hamlets, while you get to grips with the game’s combat. Despite whatever the name Soulframe might suggest, this is not a Souls-like. Combat is approachable, with a satisfying and rewarding parry window that lets you feel powerful without these opening moments feeling like a complete walkover. Depending on the Pact you’ve chosen, you have three different abilities to utilise, though only one of these is unlocked at the opening.

Where things suddenly get more difficult is when you come across a group of Ode. A batch of different warriors and machinery suddenly make things much more fraught, forcing you to focus attacks, dodge, block and parry, while trying to control the space and avoid ranged attacks at the same time. It feels excellent, giving you lots to manage, while giving weight and strength to each of your blows. That’s then further complicated by the addition of Combat Arts, both weapon specific and more generic, such as Smite, which you can sometimes leverage to strike at an enemy’s soul.

The Ode have a penchant for capturing cute and furry creatures, and through the opening hours you’ll relish saving deer, rabbits and squirrels from their nefarious clutches, while seeking to purify and heal the land that the Ode seem intent on destroying. I don’t know why, but it really reminded me of Sonic the Hedgehog saving animals from Robotnik – in the best way possible. We’ll have to see if there’s a spiky blue armour set to complete the vibes.

Through the opening, you meet Orlick the Bicameral, a ghostly writer with a hooded baby on his shoulder that occasionally whispers in his ear. His ephemeral form is searching for his quill, and once you return it, he’ll join you in the Nightfold, your home base that sits in a watery pocket dimension. He serves as your spirit guide when you’re exploring, providing spots of exposition and insight, before using his writing prowess to record your greatest deeds, though it is, in reality, just a framing device that gives you a list of secondary tasks to complete to grab some additional spoils.

His design is indicative of Digital Extremes’ idiosyncratic outlook, and just like Warframe, there’s nothing that looks or feels quite like this. From the different Ode warriors through creatures like Avakot, a leafy little chap with allergies, to the Torment Stag, the first corrupted boss, it does skew closer to the creations of FromSoftware, but there’s still an overarching individuality and slightly off-kilter outlook that infuses the art direction throughout.

That’s especially true when it comes to the armour sets you can equip; they don’t carry the same wholly alien look of its predecessor, but they definitely don’t adhere to your traditional Western medieval fantasy, drawing instead on Celtic mythology and iconography, wrapped with a tinge of Warframe’s sci-fi trappings.

Soulframe looks fantastic. The fact that this is considered an early build is astounding, and it already feels, at least at the outset, like a AAA action game. The quality of the visuals and the level design is intricate, particularly when it comes to exploring the Undercity dungeons that lurk beneath the beautiful arable fantasy, and through the opening hours you’ll repeatedly marvel at what beauty the DE team have brought to bear.

Unsurprisingly, you can purchase armour sets, weaponry and various other bits and bobs from the store, with two kinds of currency, one premium in the shape of Arcs, while the other, Dracs, can be earned in-game. There’s also plenty to find and equip from defeating enemies and exploring dungeons out in the world. If you’re coming from Warframe, you’ll know that Digital Extremes are not the kind of company to nickel and dime players, and I’d expect that you can play the entire game without spending a penny. That’s a good deal, whatever your expectations, but Soulframe looks as though it’ll more than meet them.

Soulframe already feels like a meaningful and worthy update to the Warframe formula, with a setting that begs to be explored and experienced. Fortunately, PC players will be able to dive into the Preludes open beta from Friday, 6th November.

items.title: Soulframe to launch into free open alpha this week, as Warframe devs go head-to-head with WoW: Forever
items.summary: Soulframe's new update will allow anyone who wants to to jump into the game, refreshes the onboarding with a vast corrupted map, and adds a Pact to unlock.
items.content:
Image credit: Digital Extremes News by Connor Makar Reporter Published on Nov. 2, 2026, 11:17 a.m. 10 comments Follow Soulframe Prioritise us on Google Soulframe's Preludes (its own version of an alpha) is finally opening its doors to the whole world ahead of the Verse of the Veilands update. Starting this week, anyone who wants to can simply download the game and hop in, no invite required.

The date this happens is an interesting one: 6th November. That's two days after the release of World of Warcraft: Forever and the same week as Old School RuneScape 's Hardcore worlds, so it's suddenly become a pretty packed month for MMO enthusiasts.

This comes after three years of closed testing for the fantasy action MMORPG, which players have been able to gradually see firsthand through sporadic invites. With Soulframe suffering delays since its first reveal, brief invite events have already occurred over this period. Even locked away, the game has received multiple substantial updates over the years, including new quests, Pacts (classes), factions and so on.

As for what newcomers to Soulframe can look forward to when Soulframe opens its doors, the Verse of the Veillands update is bringing a total overhaul of the map progression system this month. After the completion of an early quest, players are introduced to a corrupted landscape, the Veillands, which they must purify.

As you do so, new resources will be obtainable and side activities like fishing will be unlocked. You'll also be able to train up a small wolf pet into a full-on mount in the process. Previously, players were just thrust into the open world to explore and figure things out as they go, so this should provide something of an introduction to the game's open map. It won't be totally finished when released mind you, with updates to the Veillands system coming in the future.

On top of that, there's a new Pact called the Ode Shrike coming with the update. It's a tricksy trapper with spikes, balloon snares, bombs and chains to disrupt enemies as you whittle them down.

Could this be enough to win people over to Digital Extreme's newest project? Time will tell - but in the meantime its long-lasting sci-fi MMO Warframe is taking players to the Tau system in a major next step in the game's narrative this December. It comes with a detective noir inspired main quest, playable warframe, and even an in-universe Poker equivalent.

items.title: Warframe: Tau Coming In December
items.summary: Your remarkable journey is about to lead to an era-defining trip to the Tau System, where new worlds ripe for exploration are waiting. Jump back into Warframe today and get ready to experience our most expansive update ever this December. 6
items.content:
Your remarkable journey is about to lead to an era-defining trip to the Tau System, where new worlds ripe for exploration are waiting. Jump back into Warframe today and get ready to experience our most expansive update ever this December.

67TH WARFRAME: BRYSKO

Hit the streets of Fornax as Brysko, the world-weary, noir-inspired detective brought to life with an inner monologue voiced by Matt Mercer. Enforce your own brand of street justice with an indomitable suite of Abilities, trusty Hound Companion and signature armaments like the Rain & Shine Fist Weapons and Corecracker Exalted Pistol. Brysko also introduces the first in a new class of premium Customizations: the Chimera Skin. As with a Protoframe, you'll be able to switch between his Warframe and Chimera aspects on the fly for a more Sentient appearance and voice-acted dialogue.

TAU STAR CHART

Your evolution continues in a new region of space beyond anything you've ever known: the Tau System. While there will remain much to do in the Origin System going forward, you'll also be able to enter Missions and explore new worlds across Tau. December will start you off with the mob-run ring city of Fornax, as well as the badlands of Perita, with many more planned for future updates.

PERITA

Although Perita thrived following the events of The Old Peace, its ecosystem has since collapsed into a hostile desert populated by feuding clans of Dazannah — and where both resources and allies are notoriously difficult to come by. With the last unconquered clan facing existential peril, its chieftain’s young son, Catulast, seeks help from its ancient foe, the Tenno. Will you brave the wasteland and answer its call?

items.content:

Nidus Prime

A relentless embodiment of the Infestation, Nidus Prime thrives in the chaos of the battle, growing stronger with every mutation. Harness his parasitic powers to ensnare enemies, unleash devastating attacks and bolster his own survivability. With no conventional shields to rely on, Nidus Prime is an excellent choice for Tenno who prefer an aggressive, ability-driven playstyle that rewards you the longer you stay in the fight.

Saryn Prime

A deadly plague given form, Saryn Prime spreads toxic devastation across the battlefield, leaving few enemies untouched. Infect foes with corrosive spores, empower your weapons with lethal toxins and unleash waves of viral destruction upon entire groups. Her exceptional area-of-effect damage makes her an excellent choice for Tenno who enjoy overwhelming enemies and clearing large crowds with ease.

items.title: "Devourer" Single Release
items.summary: The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for y
items.content:
The right tunes can make all the difference when travelling afar, and your upcoming journey to the Tau System is no exception. Fortunately, we've just made another stellar musical track from the ingenious Warframe Sound Team available for your listening pleasure on major streaming platforms. "Devourer," was first heard during the Epoch Operation: Taubound Official Gameplay Teaser. Influenced by slow, heavy metal from the likes of Black Sabbath, it features lyrics "sung" in Voidtongue, the terrifyingly enigmatic language of the Untime. This was a deliberate choice, recalling the memorable moment from 2023's Whispers in the Walls Quest when you took control of one of Albrecht Entrati's Vessels for the first time. Here, these elements combine for a musical experience that feels as massive and imposing as your latest endeavors ahead of Warframe: Tau, coming later this year.

Where can I listen?

You can listen to "Devourer" on:

items.title: October in Warframe
items.summary: As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following e
items.content:
As the seasons change, so does the Origin System. And this October is no exception, with plenty of seasonal, returning, and brand new additions to occupy you as we draw ever closer to Warframe: Tau later this year. Watch for the following events this month:

EPOCH OPERATION: TAUBOUND

October 15 - November 17 A unique event unlike anything you've experienced to date, Epoch Operation: Taubound offers all eligible Tenno the chance to become a part of Warframe history. If you want to help open up a path to the Tau System, be sure to have your account ready by completing the "Vor's Prize" Quest before October 15. Players looking to pilot their Vessel for the first time can also complete The Hex and The Old Peace in order to access a new, permanent Prologue Quest setting up the Road to Tau. For full event details – including prerequisites and more – click here.

NIGHTS OF NABERUS

October 1 @ 11 a.m. ET - November 2 @ 11 a.m. ET Spooky season returns to the Origin System during our annual Halloween-inspired event, with Daughter releasing her inventory of new and returning seasonal Customizations in exchange for Mother Tokens. While Baro Ki'Teer will mark the occasion in the same unsettling fashion as last year (IYKYK), we're also mixing it up by bringing back the Hallowed Nightmares Tactical Alert, allowing you to face off against the fearsome Jack O'Naut for even more Naberus treats. For all the harrowing details, check out our Halloween 2026 Events post.

NEW GAME MODE: THE ICEBIND

October 7 Originally intended to ship alongside Iceblade of Narin as "Glacial Defiance," our new 6-player game mode was ultimately delayed to allow for additional development time and renamed to The Icebind. Accessible in-game starting October 7, these challenging, high-level Missions can be played up to three times weekly, allowing you to put your teamwork (and Loadouts) to the test for valuable Rewards. Visit the official Warframe Forums to learn more about the delay, and further details of the game mode itself.

PRINCESS MARGARET CANCER FOUNDATION QUEST

October 1 - October 31 PMCF Quest (formerly Quest to Conquer Cancer) returns for another October full of special Community streams, donation incentives and Conquera Customizations. Join us all month long and help support The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation light the way towards a world free from the fear of cancer. Visit the Warframe PMCF Quest webpage for more information or donate directly here.
